raw_response:
I farm 200 mu, but with only two people in the house I cannot make every mu too labor-heavy. So this year I will still keep wheat-maize as the main system on the better land, because I know that cycle best and it keeps income steadier. I’ll put 120 mu into winter wheat followed by summer maize on the same 120 mu. Millet is cheaper to manage, so I’ll keep 50 mu of that on the drier ground as a safer crop. Cabbage makes money if the market is good, but it needs more water, fertilizer, and spraying, so I’ll only do 30 mu. That way I still have some higher-value crop, but I don’t tie up too much cash or labor.

For fertilizer, I won’t cut too hard. In my experience, saving a little on fertilizer can cost a lot in yield, especially on wheat and cabbage. But I also won’t push too high because pumping water and buying inputs for 200 mu adds up fast. On wheat I’ll do base plus one topdress, same idea for maize. Millet I’ll keep lighter because that crop can handle poorer land better. Cabbage I’ll manage more carefully with more fertilizer and more irrigation, but only on limited area because two people cannot watch too much cabbage properly. For field work I’ll rely on machinery and some hired help at busy times, especially the tight wheat harvest to maize planting window.
